summary: A [National Data Governance Policy](2026-07-27-eswatini-validates-national-data-governance-policy) is targeted for completion before end-2026, with government undecided between a standalone law and amendments to existing legislation.
developments:
A first national workshop ran in April 2026 and the policy was validated in July, on a procurement issued through a continental alliance in 2025 ([validation](2026-07-27-eswatini-validates-national-data-governance-policy), [workshop](2026-04-30-eswatini-first-national-data-policy-workshop), [procurement](2025-07-25 RFP - Eswatini National Data Policy (Smart Africa))).

The minister told the Senate the completion target and stated that government has not decided between a standalone data-governance law and amendments to what exists; the target was put as aspirational in debate rather than as a statutory deadline ([senate](2026-08-10-eswatini-senate-data-governance-policy)).

That undecided question matters more than the date: the country already has a data protection Act, so whether data governance sits inside it or beside it decides which authority enforces what.

summary: No [national artificial-intelligence strategy or statute](2026-08-04-eswatini-online-media-publishing-guidelines-2026) is held, and two instruments now carry artificial-intelligence rules while neither is an artificial-intelligence instrument.
developments:
The finding is stated in coverage of the online media guidelines: rules on the technology are arriving inside instruments written for something else ([absence](2026-08-04-eswatini-online-media-publishing-guidelines-2026)).

A national fourth-industrial-revolution strategy framed the prime minister's address to a global artificial-intelligence governance dialogue in Geneva ([strategy](2026-07-06-eswatini-champions-human-centred-ai)), so the country argues a position internationally on the strength of an instrument that is not about artificial intelligence either.

summary: [Cybersecurity, critical infrastructure, e-commerce and artificial-intelligence legislation](2025-08-04-eswatini-ramps-up-tech-reform-legislation-5g) was named as forthcoming alongside the capital's smart-city deployment.
developments:
Four instruments were named together in August 2025 ([legislation](2025-08-04-eswatini-ramps-up-tech-reform-legislation-5g)).

None has entered the base since as a draft, a tabling or an enactment. Naming a legislative programme alongside a deployment of 59 camera systems and a fifth-generation network is the sequence worth recording: the deployment is in progress and the four laws that would govern it are a list.

summary: The [Data Protection Act 2022](2022-03-04 Eswatini Data Protection Act 2022 (Act No. 5 of 2022)) has been effective since March 2022, and its gazetted text names a Commission while the regulator describes itself as the designated Agency.
developments:
The Act was gazetted and took effect on 4 March 2022. The mismatch between the body the statute names and the body describing itself as designated is recorded rather than resolved ([Act](2022-03-04 Eswatini Data Protection Act 2022 (Act No. 5 of 2022))).

The Act is being read in press accounts as exposing online naming and shaming to a substantial penalty; that is an account of legal exposure rather than an enforcement action, and no complaint, ruling or authority statement is held ([exposure](2026-08-16-eswatiniobserver-data-protection-act-online-shaming)).

A statute whose enforcing body is ambiguous on the face of the record is a limit on everything the protection cells below can say.

summary: [Online Media Publishing Guidelines 2026](2026-08-04-eswatini-online-media-publishing-guidelines-2026) are stated by the ministry as complete in development, and [restrictions on children reaching harmful content](2026-08-19-times-eswatini-childrens-social-media-access) were raised in the Senate with no instrument behind them.
developments:
The ministry stated development of the guidelines is complete, and used the same account to state that implementation, enforcement and oversight of data protection are vested in the regulator rather than itself ([guidelines](2026-08-04-eswatini-online-media-publishing-guidelines-2026)).

A senator asked during a Senate debate what prevents minors reaching harmful content; the answer was that two offices are working together on online-content regulation. No instrument, timetable, age-verification method or definition of harmful content is stated, and no draft is held ([question](2026-08-19-times-eswatini-childrens-social-media-access)).

Guidelines complete but unpublished, and content regulation that exists only as an answer in debate, are the two forms this unit's regulation of platforms takes.

summary: The authority [opened its first major investigation](2026-06-24-home-affairs-investigated-for-sensitive-data-breach), into a ministry that [published unblurred national identity documents](2026-06-24-home-affairs-investigated-for-sensitive-data-breach) and missed the 72-hour breach-notification duty.
developments:
The investigation was opened in June 2026, following an awareness campaign in February and a lender assessment naming digital transformation as key to growth ([investigation](2026-06-24-home-affairs-investigated-for-sensitive-data-breach), [campaign](2026-02-03-eswatini-launches-data-protection-campaign), [assessment](2025-07-31 Eswatini Economic Update - Digital Transformation Key to Unlocking Growth)).

The breach was the ministry's own publication of unblurred identity documents, and it missed the statutory 72-hour notification ([breach](2026-06-24-home-affairs-investigated-for-sensitive-data-breach)).

The ICT ministry stated on the record that implementation, enforcement and oversight are vested in the regulator and not in itself, which settles the mandate question in practice even as the statute's naming of the body remains unresolved ([mandate](2026-08-04-eswatini-online-media-publishing-guidelines-2026)).

A first investigation opening against a government ministry, rather than a private controller, is the strongest single fact about this authority in the record.

The authority has used its powers: [three enforcement notices under section 41 of the Act are published, two in June 2024 against a mobile operator and an insurer and one in March 2025 against the science and technology park](2024-01-01-eswatini-dpa-enforcement). No register of complaints, breach notifications or registered controllers accompanies them.

summary: [Advisory guidelines on health data](2026-07-28-times-eswatini-esccom-health-data-guidelines) went to validation workshops, [sector guidelines](2026-08-11-eswatini-data-protection-financial-sector-breaches) were validated over a week, and [biometric gate passes](2025-07-23-outcry-over-digital-gate-pass-in-schools) were deployed in schools without ministry approval.
developments:
Health-data guidelines opened validation workshops in July 2026 ([health](2026-07-28-times-eswatini-esccom-health-data-guidelines)), and sector guidelines were validated at a week-long workshop in August; no breach count, penalty or enforcement action is published behind the regulator's ranking, and the draft guidelines are not held ([sector](2026-08-11-eswatini-data-protection-financial-sector-breaches)).

Some public schools deployed biometric gate passes without education ministry approval, charging about E200 per pupil ([schools](2025-07-23-outcry-over-digital-gate-pass-in-schools)).

Guidelines being validated at sector level while individual schools are already collecting children's biometrics for a fee, unapproved, is the gap between the regime being written and the practice on the ground.

summary: [Regional transfers are permitted under conditions](2022-03-04 Eswatini Data Protection Act 2022 (Act No. 5 of 2022)) by the Data Protection Act, while a [United States bilateral health agreement](2026-08-20-von-eswatini-us-health-funding-deal-pathogen-data) has data-sharing terms that remain unpublished.
developments:
The Act permits transfers within the regional bloc under conditions, which is an adequacy model written into the statute ([bloc](2022-03-04 Eswatini Data Protection Act 2022 (Act No. 5 of 2022))).

The health memorandum was announced in August 2026. A federal complaint records that the State Department entered into dozens of such bilateral agreements between December 2025 and February 2026, each typically a memorandum plus at least one further data-sharing agreement, that a freedom-of-information request of December 2025 covers this country's agreements, and that the department published a subset of the memoranda in March 2026 and then withdrew public access. The data-sharing terms remain unpublished ([agreement](2026-08-20-von-eswatini-us-health-funding-deal-pathogen-data)).

So the statute governs regional transfers on published conditions and the largest bilateral transfer arrangement runs on terms nobody outside the parties can read.

A regional federated know-your-customer layer is being funded: technical assistance was announced in August 2025 to connect national digital identity systems across 16 member states over the existing regional settlement and immediate-clearing payment systems ([framework](2025-08-22-cross-border-digital-identity-framework)). The announcement is the implementing partners' rather than the regional secretariat's, and names no Eswatini commitment, date or instrument.

summary: The prime minister [first dismissed a memorandum with a hyperscaler, then acknowledged in writing that Cabinet had approved it](2026-04-13-the-real-google-problem-in-eswatini-is-not-the-mou).
developments:
A former minister defended the memorandum publicly and the attorney-general confirmed that Cabinet and legal consultation preceded signature ([defence](2026-04-10-former-minister-defends-google-mou), [account](2026-04-13-the-real-google-problem-in-eswatini-is-not-the-mou)).

The published analysis argues the memorandum was not the real problem. What the exchange establishes for this frame is narrower and sufficient: a head of government publicly denied and then confirmed the existence of an approved instrument, in writing, and that correction happened because the question was pressed in public.

summary: More than [E1.06bn of lender financing was approved](2026-07-19-eswatini-1-06-billion-world-bank-digital-funding) for a digital project, reported at US$65m, after the opportunity was [noted as absent from the prime minister year-end statement](2026-01-04-the-absent-agenda-eswatini-digital-imperative).
developments:
The financing was approved in mid-2026 and converted in the source at E16.37 to the dollar; the ministry's own quarterly report behind it is not held ([financing](2026-07-19-eswatini-1-06-billion-world-bank-digital-funding), [appraisal](2026-06-08-worldbank-padhi01184-digital-eswatini-project), [project](2026-06-15-wb-swz-001-digital-eswatini-project)).

A commentary in January 2026 noted the digital-transformation opportunity as omitted from the prime minister's 2025 year-end statement ([omission](2026-01-04-the-absent-agenda-eswatini-digital-imperative)).

The project is the vehicle for the electronic identity, the public-institution connectivity target, the short-code service access and the change-agent training recorded separately — so one operation carries most of the forward programme.

summary: [Digital transformation was named a priority area](2026-08-04-eswatini-taiwan-bilaterals-digital-innovation) at a leaders' meeting with a bilateral partner in Taipei.
developments:
The meeting's own date is not established and the report is dated August 2026 ([meeting](2026-08-04-eswatini-taiwan-bilaterals-digital-innovation)).

No memorandum, workstream, value or timetable is named. Against a unit whose forward programme rests on one lender operation and one hyperscaler memorandum, a named priority area at a leaders' meeting is the whole of this bilateral relationship on the digital record.

summary: The [cost of data as a share of income per head](2025-08-04-eswatini-ramps-up-tech-reform-legislation-5g) sits above the international affordability threshold.
developments:
The finding is stated in an August 2025 account and nothing has moved it since ([affordability](2025-08-04-eswatini-ramps-up-tech-reform-legislation-5g)).

It is the constraint under the usage gap recorded separately — mobile coverage substantially exceeds mobile-internet use — and no tariff instrument, subsidy or device-financing scheme appears anywhere in this ledger to address it.

summary: [Mobile coverage against mobile-internet use](2026-07-22-independentnews-digital-eswatini-project-leadership) has not moved, while a [smart-city deployment](2025-08-04-eswatini-ramps-up-tech-reform-legislation-5g) fits a fifth-generation network, 59 camera systems and public wireless access in the capital.
developments:
The coverage and usage figures come from the ICT ministry, given at a change-management workshop for the digital project ([coverage](2026-07-22-independentnews-digital-eswatini-project-leadership), [reform](2025-08-04-eswatini-ramps-up-tech-reform-legislation-5g)).

The capital's deployment fits a fifth-generation network, 59 artificial-intelligence-enabled cameras and public wireless access ([deployment](2025-08-04-eswatini-ramps-up-tech-reform-legislation-5g)).

No lawful basis, retention rule or oversight arrangement for the camera network is stated anywhere, and the four laws named as forthcoming alongside it — including critical infrastructure and artificial intelligence — have not appeared.

summary: The regulator [proposed raising the minimum service standard from 2 Mbps to 10 Mbps](2026-07-20-eswatini-esccom-10mbps), and [free statutory complaint adjudication](2026-08-04-esccom-consumer-guide-type-approved-equipment) runs on windows of one to six months by sector.
developments:
The proposal was issued as a public notice in July 2026 ([proposal](2026-07-20-eswatini-esccom-10mbps)).

Adjudication is free under the 2013 communications Act, with windows of one month for post and courier, three for broadcasting and six for telecommunications; these are structural provisions of the Act rather than dated state ([adjudication](2026-08-04-esccom-consumer-guide-type-approved-equipment)).

A six-month window for a telecommunications complaint is long enough that the remedy is unlikely to reach the problem it was raised about, and no complaint volume or outcome series is published.

summary: [International capacity rose from 47 to 72 Gbps](2026-02-13-optical-fibre-rollout-strengthens-business-ecosystem), above target, and [1,031 public institutions](2026-07-22-independentnews-digital-eswatini-project-leadership) are targeted for connection under the digital project.
developments:
The capacity increase was reported in February 2026 as above target ([capacity](2026-02-13-optical-fibre-rollout-strengthens-business-ecosystem), [rollout](2025-08-04-eswatini-ramps-up-tech-reform-legislation-5g)).

The institution target was stated at the project's change-management workshop ([institutions](2026-07-22-independentnews-digital-eswatini-project-leadership)).

A landlocked country raising international capacity by half in a reporting period is a real gain; it is also why the satellite gateway recorded separately is framed as reducing dependence on cross-border fibre.

summary: A [government satellite gateway was commissioned](2026-04-28-eswatini-commissions-starlink-satellite-gateway) to reach mountainous and remote areas and reduce dependence on cross-border fibre, and a [business reseller channel](2025-07-30-paratus-eswatini-drives-starlink-business-adoption) launched as a joint venture.
developments:
The gateway was commissioned in April 2026, its stated purpose reaching mountainous and remote areas and reducing dependence on cross-border fibre ([gateway](2026-04-28-eswatini-commissions-starlink-satellite-gateway)).

A joint venture launched as an authorised business reseller in July 2025 ([reseller](2025-07-30-paratus-eswatini-drives-starlink-business-adoption)).

A government-commissioned gateway is an unusual arrangement — most units in this frame record licensing and resale rather than state operation — and no capacity, coverage or cost figure is published for it.

summary: A government assessment finds ministries [depend heavily on the National Data Centre with no internal fallback](2026-05-21-critical-state-information-at-risk-in-9-govt-ministries).
developments:
The assessment finding is that dependence is heavy and internal fallback absent ([assessment](2026-05-21-critical-state-information-at-risk-in-9-govt-ministries), [centre](2021-01-01 The National Data Centre - Royal Science and Technology Park)).

No capacity, tenancy, availability or redundancy figure is published for the facility itself. A single national facility with no ministry-level fallback is a concentration risk the state's own assessment names and nothing on record answers.

summary: The ICT minister [met a Gulf clean-energy firm](2026-02-06-eswatini-explores-green-energy-for-national-data-centre) to discuss dedicated supply for the National Data Centre, and nothing has been signed.
developments:
The meeting took place at an international government summit in February 2026 and nothing was signed ([supply](2026-02-06-eswatini-explores-green-energy-for-national-data-centre), [discussions](2026-02-06-eswatini-explores-green-energy-for-national-data-centre)).

Dedicated power for the single national facility on which ministries have no fallback is the right problem to be working on. That it is at the stage of an unsigned discussion is the state of it.

The published tariff schedule is where this can be tested, and it does not carry the category: [an average increase of 13.61 per cent was approved for 2026/27 and revised down to 11.74 per cent after special government funding, effective 1 April 2026](2025-01-01-eswatini-electricity-tariff-structure), across a lifeline domestic band and time-of-use commercial tariffs, with no data-centre or large-load category anywhere in it.

summary: A Digital Landscape Assessment found [ministry data backup and ICT maintenance](2026-05-21-critical-state-information-at-risk-in-9-govt-ministries) wanting and [government systems not interoperable](2026-05-21-critical-state-information-at-risk-in-9-govt-ministries), with critical state information at risk in nine ministries.
developments:
The assessment was received and endorsed by the ICT ministry, so the finding is the government's own rather than an outside audit ([backups](2026-05-21-critical-state-information-at-risk-in-9-govt-ministries)).

Interoperability between government systems is a finding of the same assessment ([interoperability](2026-05-21-critical-state-information-at-risk-in-9-govt-ministries)).

A state that has endorsed an assessment saying critical information is at risk in nine ministries, while running everything on one data centre with no ministry-level fallback, has documented its own exposure. The assessment is also what the electronic-government strategy is being founded on, which is the right response and has not yet produced a strategy.

summary: A [regional cybersecurity framework](2026-07-30-independentnews-sadc-ccbg-cyber-frameworks) was finalised and approved at a subcommittee hosted in-country, and a [national awareness month](2025-10-07-eswatini-calls-for-collaboration-to-protect-cyber-space) was opened by the prime minister.
developments:
The regional framework was finalised and approved by a central bank governors' subcommittee at a meeting in the country in July 2026 ([framework](2026-07-30-independentnews-sadc-ccbg-cyber-frameworks)).

Cybersecurity awareness month was opened by the prime minister in October 2025 ([awareness](2025-10-07-eswatini-calls-for-collaboration-to-protect-cyber-space)).

Neither is a national instrument. The country has no cybersecurity statute — one was named as forthcoming a year ago — no incident response team on record, and no incident, caseload or capability figure anywhere in this ledger.

Enforcement has a unit behind it: [a police digital forensic unit and cyber task team had made 87 arrests and submitted 528 dockets to the prosecutions director by October 2025](2025-10-06-natcom-praises-digital-forensic-unit), working on mobile money fraud, fake wallet schemes, online loan scams and rental scams. [Over E8.5 million was involved in cyber-related crime in the twelve months to 30 September 2025](2025-10-06-natcom-praises-digital-forensic-unit).

progress: Mixed, electronic identity planned for 2027 while national card production was suspended for five months
summary: [Electronic identities are planned](2026-06-24-ict-trains-change-agents-e1-2bn-digitization) under the digital project for a 2027 rollout, and [national card production resumed](2026-02-22-home-affairs-resumes-id-card-production) in February 2026 after a suspension from late September 2025.
developments:
Electronic identities are planned for a 2027 rollout, on a readiness report first published in 2024 ([plan](2026-06-24-ict-trains-change-agents-e1-2bn-digitization), [readiness](2024-11-22 Eswatini unveils readiness report for digital ID, transformation push)).

Production of the existing national card was suspended in late September 2025 and resumed on 22 February 2026; the card is not a digital identity ([resumption](2026-02-22-home-affairs-resumes-id-card-production), [regulation](2024-07-22 Risk of human rights infringement as Eswatini rushes to regulate the ICT sector)).

No cause, backlog figure or remediation is published for the five-month suspension. A credential system that stopped issuing for five months, in the same period its ministry published unblurred identity documents and missed the breach-notification duty, is the base on which the 2027 electronic identity is to be built.

summary: The central bank is [standing up a national electronic know-your-customer registry](2025-09-26-eswatini-national-ekyc-system) to digitise identity verification.
developments:
The registry was reported in September 2025 ([registry](2025-09-26-eswatini-national-ekyc-system)).

No go-live, participant count or governing instrument is published. It would be the country's first authentication layer, and it is being built by the central bank rather than by the identity or ICT authorities — so the first working identity verification in the state may sit inside the financial regulator.

summary: A [National FinTech Strategy 2025-2030](2025-12-07-fintech-strategy-to-transform-eswatini-digital-future) was launched by the central bank governor and the finance minister, above a [digital currency design paper](2024-01-01-cbe-eswatini-digital-lilangeni-design-paper) published in 2024.
developments:
The strategy was launched in December 2025, framed around reducing reliance on cash ([strategy](2025-12-07-fintech-strategy-to-transform-eswatini-digital-future), [cash](2025-12-05-fintech-to-reduce-cash-reliance)).

The design paper is not an issuance decision, and no pilot, launch date or governance arrangement follows it ([paper](2024-01-01-cbe-eswatini-digital-lilangeni-design-paper)).

The central bank's annual integrated reports are held for two successive years, the later superseding a payment-switch participation series the base had carried from earlier reporting ([report](2026-01-01-cbe-eswatini-annual-integrated-report-2025-26), [prior](2025-01-01-cbe-eswatini-annual-integrated-report-2024-25)).

The settlement layer under all of it is old and undocumented since: the interbank payment and settlement system runs under a rulebook adopted by its steering committee in May 2007 ([rulebook](2007-05-swipss-rules-and-procedures)), and the central bank describes its role as facilitating development and overseeing the safety and soundness of national payment systems ([mandate](2025-01-01-central-bank-eswatini-national-payment-systems)). No revision of the rulebook, and no volume or value statistic for the system, is published.

summary: The [payment switch launched fast payments](2025-01-14 Phil Mnisi - Eswatini Payment Switch Fast Payments product launch) as phase one of three, and [35 post offices opened for government-service payments](2025-09-26-eswatini-post-office-based-govt-payment-system).
developments:
Fast payments launched as phase one of three; no source held confirms whether the remaining five participants went live as expected by end-January 2025 ([launch](2025-01-14 Phil Mnisi - Eswatini Payment Switch Fast Payments product launch), [explainer](2025-09-28-eswatini-payment-switch-explainer)).

Thirty-five post offices were opened for government-service payments in September 2025 ([post offices](2025-09-26-eswatini-post-office-based-govt-payment-system)).

A rail whose participant list cannot be confirmed eighteen months after phase one, alongside a physical over-the-counter channel, is where person-to-government payment actually stands here.

summary: [Migration of regional low-value flows to a bloc settlement system](2026-07-21-egypt-eswatini-deepen-banking-cooperation) is reported under way with no timetable, and [accession to a continental payment system](2026-07-21-egypt-eswatini-deepen-banking-cooperation) was discussed with a bilateral partner.
developments:
The migration is reported as under way with no timetable, volume, value or mandating instrument given ([migration](2026-07-21-egypt-eswatini-deepen-banking-cooperation)).

The central bank governor discussed leveraging another country's experience to accelerate continental accession ([accession](2026-07-21-egypt-eswatini-deepen-banking-cooperation)).

Both are cross-border commitments stated in the same bilateral meeting account, and neither has a date.

summary: A finance portfolio committee [tabled a report on bank transaction charges](2026-07-29-cbe-called-to-probe-bank-charges-eswatini) and [recommended the central bank report a comparative benchmark](2026-07-29-cbe-called-to-probe-bank-charges-eswatini) within 30 days of adoption.
developments:
The report was tabled in July 2026 ([report](2026-07-29-cbe-called-to-probe-bank-charges-eswatini)) with a recommendation that the central bank produce a comparative benchmark of charges within 30 days of adoption ([benchmark](2026-07-29-cbe-called-to-probe-bank-charges-eswatini)).

No adoption date, benchmark or central bank response is on record. Legislative scrutiny of transaction pricing is rare in this frame and worth recording as such; whether it produced anything is unestablished.

summary: [Account ownership](2025-08-10-mobile-money-drives-financial-inclusion-growth) rose on a global survey cited in the record, against a [cash share of person-to-business payments](2025-08-05 Robust DPI inevitable for Eswatini's economic, jobs boom - World Bank) the lender assessed as high.
developments:
The account ownership figure is a reference-study figure, cited rather than absorbed ([ownership](2025-08-10-mobile-money-drives-financial-inclusion-growth)), and the cash share comes from a lender assessment of digital public infrastructure ([cash](2025-08-05 Robust DPI inevitable for Eswatini's economic, jobs boom - World Bank)).

The mobile money platform migrated to a cloud-native vendor platform across four markets; the performance figures are the vendor's own and no downtime, cost or subscriber-impact figure is stated ([migration](2026-08-21-tan-ericsson-mtn-momo-cloud-migration)).

Neither uptake figure is a domestic series, so what the payment switch and the post-office channel changed cannot be measured from this base.

summary: A [compulsory civil register](1998-12-01-eswatini-births-marriages-deaths-registration-act-1983) has run since January 1984 under a 1983 statute, and nothing in the base shows it has been digitised.
developments:
The register commenced on 6 January 1984 under a births, marriages and deaths registration Act, administered by a registrar in the home affairs ministry ([statute](1998-12-01-eswatini-births-marriages-deaths-registration-act-1983), [assessment](2025-08-05 Robust DPI inevitable for Eswatini's economic, jobs boom - World Bank)).

It is a paper-based statute and nothing shows digitisation. The electronic identity planned for 2027 would therefore be built on a register whose current form is unrecorded, in the ministry whose card production stopped for five months and which is under investigation for a data breach.

summary: A [proposed DNA requirement for birth certificates](2026-07-14-dna-plan-could-swallow-e126m-of-home-affairs-budget) is costed at about E126m a year, roughly 46 per cent of the home affairs budget.
developments:
The costing is reported against the ministry's budget ([proposal](2026-07-14-dna-plan-could-swallow-e126m-of-home-affairs-budget)).

It is a proposal only. Requiring genetic testing to register a birth would be the most invasive civil-registration rule in this frame, and the account that reaches the base is about its cost rather than its lawful basis, consent model or effect on registration rates.

The improvement work has a structure behind it: a national steering committee and technical working group were established under a continental mentorship programme whose second phase launched in February 2022 ([programme](2022-02-12-eswatini-crvs-phase-two-launch)), with a university partner supporting the government since 2015 on foreign health-programme funding ([support](2022-09-28-icap-eswatini-civil-registration)). [Over 10,000 of the births occurring in 2021 were registered late](2022-09-28-icap-eswatini-civil-registration).

summary: [Community health services moved from paper to digital records](2026-02-23 From Paper to Pixels - Digital Transformation of Community Health Services in Eswatini), and a [regional artificial-intelligence health partnership](2026-08-04-ecsa-hc-skye-africa-intelligence-partner-to-scale-ai-health-solutions) was signed in-country with a private firm.
developments:
The transition from paper to digital records in community health services is documented in February 2026 ([transition](2026-02-23 From Paper to Pixels - Digital Transformation of Community Health Services in Eswatini)).

A memorandum between a regional health body and a private firm to scale artificial-intelligence health solutions was signed in the country in August 2026 ([partnership](2026-08-04-ecsa-hc-skye-africa-intelligence-partner-to-scale-ai-health-solutions)).

Advisory guidelines on processing personal health data were still in validation workshops at that point, so the partnership and the digitisation are both ahead of the guidance meant to govern them.

Underneath the policy the record system is in place: [an open-source, government-owned electronic medical record is live at 233 sites, 73 per cent of health facilities](2026-04-07-even-on-the-rainiest-afternoons-in-eswatini), keyed on a unique identity number with role-based access and backed up in government-owned cloud systems, so a patient's history follows them between districts.

summary: [Three platforms were launched with an operator](2026-06-20-eswatini-rolls-out-digital-platforms-health-agriculture-creative) covering agriculture, health and the creative economy.
developments:
The three platforms launched together in June 2026 ([platforms](2026-06-20-eswatini-rolls-out-digital-platforms-health-agriculture-creative)).

No user count, data arrangement, custodian or public-sector role is published for any of them. Three sectoral platforms delivered through a commercial operator, in a country whose government systems its own assessment finds not interoperable, is a delivery route that works and does not connect to anything.

summary: The Auditor-General [launched a 2026-2030 strategic plan](2026-08-17-eswatini-auditor-general-ai-digital-transformation) integrating artificial intelligence, and the plan text is not held.
developments:
The plan was launched in August 2026 ([plan](2026-08-17-eswatini-auditor-general-ai-digital-transformation), [integration](2026-08-17-eswatini-audit-office-integrates-ai-in-new-strategy)).

No tool, data access, assurance standard or safeguard for audit use of artificial intelligence is stated. A supreme audit institution adopting the technology is consequential — it is the body that would otherwise audit its use elsewhere in government — and the country has no artificial-intelligence strategy or statute at all.

summary: The regulator [urged broadcasters to manage artificial intelligence and deepfakes ethically and transparently](2025-11-22-esccom-issues-ai-warning-on-deep-fakes).
developments:
The guidance was issued in November 2025 ([guidance](2025-11-22-esccom-issues-ai-warning-on-deep-fakes)).

It is guidance to a single sector, urging rather than requiring, and it is one of the two instruments that carry artificial-intelligence rules in a country with no artificial-intelligence instrument. The other is the online media guidelines.

progress: Mixed, two citizen applications live while the prime minister states a memorandum signed without proper data-protection consideration is meaningless
summary: A [citizen application](2025-05-21-eswatini-launches-new-apps-giyh-taxpal) and a [tax application](2025-05-21-eswatini-launches-new-apps-giyh-taxpal) launched together, and the prime minister told the House that a memorandum signed without proper consideration for data protection is meaningless.
developments:
Both applications launched in May 2025, for government services and for tax accounts and clearance certificates ([launch](2025-05-21-eswatini-launches-new-apps-giyh-taxpal), [applications](2025-05-21-eswatini-launches-new-apps-giyh-taxpal)).

The prime minister's own words — that the application must be watertight, that his office does not support outsourcing data to global technology companies, and that a memorandum signed without proper consideration for data protection is meaningless — are in his written responses tabled to the House of Assembly in March 2026 ([responses](2026-03-18-eswatini-observer-pm-denies-firing-ict-minister), [criticism](2025-07-04-biometricupdate-eswatini-giyh-privacy-criticism)).

An assessment count of government services available online is held ([services](2026-05-21-critical-state-information-at-risk-in-9-govt-ministries)), and an electronic-government strategy is being founded on that same assessment with nothing yet produced ([strategy](2026-05-21-critical-state-information-at-risk-in-9-govt-ministries)).

summary: [Thirty-eight constituency centres](2026-07-22-independentnews-digital-eswatini-project-leadership) are included in the digital project's connectivity target.
developments:
The centres are part of the 1,031-institution target ([centres](2026-07-22-independentnews-digital-eswatini-project-leadership)).

No timetable, service list or per-centre arrangement is published. Constituency centres are the tier at which most citizens meet the state in this country, so their inclusion in the connectivity target is the single most consequential line in it.

summary: [Short-code access to public services](2026-06-24-ict-trains-change-agents-e1-2bn-digitization) is planned so citizens without smartphones can transact, and [44 devices were handed to agricultural extension officers](2026-08-10-eswatini-sapemp-digital-equipment-extension-officers).
developments:
Short-code access is planned under the digital project specifically so citizens without smartphones can transact ([access](2026-06-24-ict-trains-change-agents-e1-2bn-digitization)). In a country where data cost sits above the affordability threshold, that is the design choice that decides whether the rest of the programme reaches anyone rural.

Forty-four devices were handed to extension officers in August 2026, with no officer total, data platform, reporting standard or custodian for the collected field data stated ([devices](2026-08-10-eswatini-sapemp-digital-equipment-extension-officers)).

Field data collected on state-issued devices with no named custodian is a data-protection question the guidelines under validation do not yet reach.

summary: A [provisional banking licence was granted](2026-07-22-letshego-digital-banking) for a transition to a full digital bank.
developments:
The provisional licence was granted and the transition is under way ([licence](2026-07-22-letshego-digital-banking)).

No capital, timetable, customer base or launch date is published. It is the only domestic digital-industry item in this ledger apart from platforms delivered by a mobile operator.

summary: The ICT minister [set a target for digitally skilled citizens](2026-02-02-300000-emaswati-needed-for-country-digital-future), and a domestic practitioner [published guidance on digital workplace transformation](2026-01-25 ICT EXPERT UNVEILS BOOK ON DIGITAL WORKPLACE TRANSFORMATION).
developments:
The target was set in February 2026 ([target](2026-02-02-300000-emaswati-needed-for-country-digital-future)) and no programme, budget or measurement method is attached to it.

A book by a domestic ICT practitioner is the only other literacy item in the ledger ([book](2026-01-25 ICT EXPERT UNVEILS BOOK ON DIGITAL WORKPLACE TRANSFORMATION)).

A national skills target with no delivery instrument behind it, in a country whose stated internet-usage and youth-unemployment rates are recorded elsewhere in this report, is an aspiration rather than a programme.

summary: [Artificial-intelligence, robotics and cybersecurity training](2026-08-06-ai-robotics-training-coming-to-innovation-hubs) was announced as the next phase at innovation hubs, and [cross-ministry change agents](2026-06-24-ict-trains-change-agents-e1-2bn-digitization) are in training for the 2027 rollout.
developments:
The hub curriculum was announced at a hub handover as the phase beyond basic digital literacy ([curriculum](2026-08-06-ai-robotics-training-coming-to-innovation-hubs)).

Change agents across ministries are in training for the digital project's 2027 rollout ([agents](2026-06-24-ict-trains-change-agents-e1-2bn-digitization)).

Neither carries a cohort size, curriculum, completion measure or placement figure. Training change agents ahead of a rollout is the correct order, and it is the only training in this unit tied to a specific delivery date.

summary: A [second community innovation hub opened](2026-08-08-govt-launches-macetjeni-ihub-to-drive-digital-innovation) in August 2026, against a stated 58 per cent internet-usage rate and 56 per cent youth unemployment.
developments:
The second hub opened in a rural region ([hub](2026-08-08-govt-launches-macetjeni-ihub-to-drive-digital-innovation), [phase](2026-08-06-ai-robotics-training-coming-to-innovation-hubs)).

It opened against a stated 58 per cent internet-usage rate and 56 per cent youth unemployment, and the account is the funding agency's own ([opening](2026-08-06-eswatini-undp-macetjeni-ihub-digital-skills)).

No financing figure was disclosed for the facility, and no user, training or enterprise-support count is published for either hub ([hubs](2026-08-07-eswatini-macetjeni-ihub-launch)). Two hubs are the country's whole physical inclusion programme.

summary: A [consumer financial survey](2026-07-24-cbe-launches-survey-financial-inclusion-eswatini) launched its 2026 round, replacing a 2018 measurement, and a [communications sector study](2026-01-19-e2-8m-study-signals-bright-2026-digital-outlook) was tendered at about E2.8m.
developments:
The survey round was launched in July 2026, replacing a measurement eight years old ([survey](2026-07-24-cbe-launches-survey-financial-inclusion-eswatini)).

The sector study tender was awarded in January 2026 ([study](2026-01-19-e2-8m-study-signals-bright-2026-digital-outlook)).

Both are commissioned measurements rather than recurring statistical series, and both are being stood up to replace figures the country has been reading from foreign reference studies — which is what the account-ownership and cash-share cells in this report rest on.

summary: A [hyperscaler memorandum](2026-04-10-former-minister-defends-google-mou) was confirmed by the attorney-general to have followed Cabinet and legal consultation, and a [specimen sharing agreement](2025-12-12-us-eswatini-health-specimen-sharing-agreement) entered into force in January 2026.
developments:
The attorney-general confirmed that Cabinet approval and legal consultation preceded signature ([confirmation](2026-04-10-former-minister-defends-google-mou), [partnership](2025-01-21-google-works-with-eswatini-to-accelerate-digital-economy)), and the country was represented at the vendor's continental summit with its citizen application showcased ([summit](2026-07-05-eswatini-digital-progress-earns-continental-spotlight), [partners](2025-01-20-insidebiz-eswatini-partners-with-google)).

The specimen sharing agreement was signed in December 2025 and entered into force on 11 January 2026. The memorandum it hangs on is not published: main texts were posted for several countries and removed, and for this country only the agreement remains posted ([agreement](2025-12-12-us-eswatini-health-specimen-sharing-agreement)).

So the hyperscaler arrangement was contested in public and its approval route confirmed, while the health arrangement's governing memorandum was published and then withdrawn.

summary: A [women digital academy](2026-07-23-eswatini-launches-africa-first-womens-digital-academy) was launched virtually under a bilateral memorandum signed at a United Nations General Assembly.
developments:
The academy launched in July 2026 under a memorandum signed at the 2025 General Assembly ([academy](2026-07-23-eswatini-launches-africa-first-womens-digital-academy)).

No cohort size, curriculum, funding or duration is published. It is the only delivered output of any Gulf arrangement in this ledger; the other, on power for the national data centre, remains an unsigned discussion.

summary: A [social registry is piloting in one of four regions](2026-06-18-world-bank-injects-e42-5-million-social-registry), with 44,683 households enrolled and targeting run on a proxy means test.
developments:
[The Shiselweni pilot covered 47,766 households, registered 44,683 of them and recorded 3,088 as vacant or non-consenting](2026-06-18-world-bank-injects-e42-5-million-social-registry), against a projected 47,260 households in the region.

[Targeting uses a proxy means test built on 20 variables from the household income and expenditure survey, and the programme carries US$2.5 million, about E42.5 million, of World Bank funding](2026-06-18-world-bank-injects-e42-5-million-social-registry); each region is to be given three months to implement.

No national rollout date, no statement of which grant programmes will draw on the registry, and no data-protection or grievance arrangement for it, are on record.

summary: An [integrated electronic case management system](2026-05-21-new-digital-court-system-case-delays) launched in August 2025 is being extended across the justice sector, with no live-service statement yet.
developments:
The system was launched by the justice ministry on 18 August 2025, beginning end-user capacity building across the sector ([system](2026-05-21-new-digital-court-system-case-delays)).

It is designed to replace paper filing with electronic case filing, virtual hearings and case tracking, and to connect the judiciary, the justice ministry, the law society, the police, the anti-corruption commission and correctional services on one platform; a development agency donated the equipment ([design](2026-05-21-new-digital-court-system-case-delays)).

Parliamentary portfolio committees were briefed on 20 May 2026, where the senate president raised the security of court files in the system ([briefing](2026-05-21-new-digital-court-system-case-delays)). No case volume, court coverage or go-live date is published.

summary: A [school education management information system went national in March 2024](2024-04-26-eswatini-launches-semis), carrying individual learner and staff records keyed to a personal identification number.
developments:
[The system was launched nationally between 19 and 22 March 2024](2024-04-26-eswatini-launches-semis), after a pilot begun in 2020 and testing in ten schools.

It replaces semi-annual paper returns entered centrally into a desktop database, carries both aggregate education data and individual learner and staff records identified by a personal identification number, and was built on an open-source platform by the education ministry with a UN agency, a university and two implementing partners ([implementation](2024-01-01-eswatini-dhis2-for-education-implementation)).

Unreliable internet, a shortage of school-owned devices and limited digital skills leave most rural primary schools collecting enrolment, attendance and learner data on paper for later entry ([constraints](2024-01-01-eswatini-dhis2-for-education-implementation)). No enrolment count or data-sharing arrangement with the population register is published.

summary: [Online filing has been compulsory since 2022](2022-05-mandating-digital-tax-tools-covid-eswatini), and the revenue service is [procuring fiscalisation and electronic invoicing](2025-05-13-daily-business-transactions-monitored-ai-tax-fraud) to close an [E4.4 billion tax gap](2025-10-29-ers-intensifies-drive-close-tax-gap).
developments:
Online filing was made compulsory for income tax payers with a zero-cash-handling payment policy; an independent evaluation found registered taxpayers 60 per cent less likely to file nil returns and 70 per cent more likely to pay once they had filed ([mandate](2022-05-mandating-digital-tax-tools-covid-eswatini)).

[The tax gap stands at E4.4 billion, with wholesale and retail the largest contributor, chiefly in value added tax](2025-10-29-ers-intensifies-drive-close-tax-gap), and the compliance improvement plan segments taxpayers four ways and names analytics and fiscalisation as the detection method.

A fiscalisation and electronic invoicing system went to the market in May 2025, specified for real-time invoice reporting, fiscal devices integrated with revenue systems and predictive targeting of high-risk taxpayers; no award, supplier or value is on record ([procurement](2025-05-13-daily-business-transactions-monitored-ai-tax-fraud)).

summary: A [master patient index integrated with the population registry](2026-01-30-disconnected-to-integrated-eswatini-healthcare-systems) now feeds a standards-based health information exchange across previously disconnected systems.
developments:
An implementing partner deployed a master patient index using deterministic and probabilistic matching with machine-learning enhancement, integrated the population registry to strengthen patient identification, and added fuzzy search for name variations ([index](2026-01-30-disconnected-to-integrated-eswatini-healthcare-systems)).

A second phase put the index behind an interoperability platform and configured a health-data-standard exchange, with separate mediators for demographic and clinical data and end-to-end testing on real workflows ([exchange](2026-01-30-disconnected-to-integrated-eswatini-healthcare-systems)).

The account is the implementing partner's rather than the ministry's, and no statement of which facilities are connected, what volume is exchanged, or under what legal basis patient data moves between them, is held.

summary: The [deeds registry is still manual](2025-08-25-eswatini-delegation-kenya-lands-benchmarking), with the registrar stating an intention to move to a fully electronic system after two study missions in five months.
developments:
A delegation from the deeds registry and the science and technology park made a five-day study visit to a neighbouring land registry in August 2025, the second such mission in five months, the first having been led by the principal secretary for natural resources and energy ([mission](2025-08-25-eswatini-delegation-kenya-lands-benchmarking)).

The registrar stated that registration and storage of deeds remain manual and that the country is working to upgrade them into a fully electronic system ([position](2025-08-25-eswatini-delegation-kenya-lands-benchmarking)).

No system, procurement, budget line or date for that upgrade is on record, and no parcel or title count is published.

summary: Company [name search and reservation run online with incorporation in a day](2025-01-01-eswatini-company-registration-procedure), and a [one-stop shop for investors opened in July 2025](2025-07-14-business-one-stop-shop-opens-july-21).
developments:
Name availability is searched and reserved through the government portal, the reservation holding for 90 days, and incorporation is processed within one day; fees run from E645 to E1,845 by nominal capital ([procedure](2025-01-01-eswatini-company-registration-procedure)).

The one-stop shop opened to the public on 21 July 2025 after a pilot from May, offering a trading licence, a taxpayer identification number, home affairs permits and science park services from one counter to investors turning over E2 million or more, or E10 million for foreign investors ([shop](2025-07-14-business-one-stop-shop-opens-july-21)).

Only one-month work permits can be applied for through it; longer permits still go to the home affairs ministry ([limit](2025-07-14-business-one-stop-shop-opens-july-21)). No register size or transaction count is published.

summary: Taxpayer identification number registration is [free but paper-based](2024-01-01-eswatini-tin-registration-procedure), on a form collected from an office or downloaded, with twelve supporting documents.
developments:
The procedure is free and administered by the revenue service under the value added tax statute, with the form collected from an office or downloaded and twelve supporting documents required, from a certified certificate of incorporation to evidence of a fixed place of business and the capacity to keep accounting records ([procedure](2024-01-01-eswatini-tin-registration-procedure)).

There is no online submission route, which sits against company registration in the same ministry running through the government portal ([company](2025-01-01-eswatini-company-registration-procedure)).

No count of registered taxpayers is published, and the underlying forms the procedure page links carry dates of April 2020.

summary: A [university computer science department](2024-01-01-uneswa-computer-science-department) names a health-informatics research group and a cybersecurity and forensics group alongside a masters programme.
developments:
The department runs undergraduate and masters programmes in computer science, information technology and information science, and lists two research groups, one in health informatics and one in cybersecurity and forensics, with pages for publications and conferences and for research grants ([department](2024-01-01-uneswa-computer-science-department)).

It also hosts an ICT fair, a deep learning event and a hackathon, and acknowledges a development agency for sponsoring student data during remote teaching ([activity](2024-01-01-uneswa-computer-science-department)).

No funding line, output count or contribution to national digital policy is stated for either group, so what the department contributes to policy is not established.

summary: A [digital readiness assessment published in November 2024](2024-11-01-eswatini-digital-readiness-assessment) places the country at the systematic stage across all six of its pillars.
developments:
The assessment was launched by the ICT ministry with a development agency in November 2024 and places the country at the systematic stage across digital public infrastructure, connectivity, government, regulation, economy and people ([assessment](2024-11-01-eswatini-digital-readiness-assessment)).

It finds that a national digital strategy is in place but that digitalisation holds only moderate political support, naming limited political prioritisation and coordination as the constraint on the government pillar ([finding](2024-11-01-eswatini-digital-readiness-assessment)).

The strategy the assessment refers to is not itself held, and no implementation plan or budget against the assessment's recommendations is published.

summary: The [tax gap stands at E4.4 billion](2025-10-29-ers-intensifies-drive-close-tax-gap), and the largest digital programme in the country runs on [E1.2 billion of external money](2026-06-23-e1-2-billion-digital-project-connect-schools-clinics-communities).
developments:
[The revenue commissioner general put the tax gap at E4.4 billion in October 2025, with wholesale and retail the largest contributor, chiefly in value added tax](2025-10-29-ers-intensifies-drive-close-tax-gap).

[The digital transformation programme carries E1.2 billion, about US$65 million, of which E648 million goes to affordable broadband and E450 million to the citizen-services component](2026-06-23-e1-2-billion-digital-project-connect-schools-clinics-communities), and it is externally financed rather than appropriated.

No domestic budget appropriation for digital transformation is held for any year, which is what leaves the programme's continuation resting on the external facility.
